Customs Act 2023: This law provides the legal authority under Section 25(1) for the government to grant duty exemptions on specific goods imported for power generation purposes.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This law provides the legal authority under Section 126(1) for the government to grant VAT exemptions on specific goods imported for power generation.
National Board of Revenue: The government issues this exemption order in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Customs Duty: For specific coal imports intended for power plants, the customs duty exceeding five percent ad valorem is exempted.
Value Added Tax: The entire amount of value added tax is exempted for the importation of coal used in public or private power generation centers, subject to specific conditions.
H.S. Code: The order specifies H.S. Code 2701.19.00 for coal eligible for duty and tax exemptions when imported for electricity generation.
Commissioner of Customs: The importer is required to submit a formal undertaking, formatted as per the appendix, to the relevant Commissioner of Customs before clearing each shipment of coal.

Certificate of Import: This document serves as a formal certificate confirming that imported coal is intended solely for electricity generation by an authorized power plant. It verifies the contractual relationship between the entity and the Government of Bangladesh for power generation purposes. The certificate mandates that the specified quantity of imported coal must be utilized exclusively within the plant for energy production.
Power Generation Entity: This is an entity that has entered into a formal contract with the Government of Bangladesh for the establishment and operation of a power plant in either the public or private sector. The entity must have already commenced commercial production to be eligible for certification regarding imported inputs.

Customs Act 2023: The Customs Act 2023 provides the legal framework under which enforcement actions are taken if imported goods are used for purposes other than those stated in the undertaking.
Imported Coal: The importer must provide a formal undertaking that the imported coal is directly related to power generation and will be used exclusively at the designated power plant. If the coal is diverted for unauthorized purposes or locations, the importer is obligated to pay all applicable duties and taxes.
